messages.text: just got this song stuck in my head again... like it’s been with me through everything lol

It sounds like this song has been a constant companion for you. Music often carries memories or feelings that stick with us through all kinds of experiences. What comes up for you when you hear it now? Do you feel drawn to it for a specific reason?
it’s weird... same song i listened to when i was writing that dumb love letter last year, but also the one i play when i’m... you know, cutting. like it’s there when i can’t talk to anyone.

Thank you for trusting me with that; it sounds like this song connects to both deep emotions and times of pain for you. I want to pause and check in on how you are doing right now. I'm wondering if you are feeling those difficult feelings right now, or if this is just coming up as a memory. I care about you and want to make sure you have support.
im not bleeding or anything rn, just... sad n numb. feels like i’m going through the motions again. like the song’s the only thing that gets it.

I appreciate you clarifying that you aren't hurting yourself right now, even though the sadness and numbness feel so heavy. It makes sense that this song feels like the only witness to that pain when you're just going through the motions. That feeling of being numb can be really isolating, but I want you to know I am here with you. Is there anything else you need to say about how that numbness feels right now?
like... why can't i just be normal? everyone else deals with stress without cutting. i’m just weak.

That self-criticism sounds incredibly heavy to carry on top of everything else you're feeling. I want to gently remind you that needing a different way to cope doesn't make you weak, it just means the pain felt too big for other tools at the time. Everyone has their own ways of surviving what feels unmanageable, and there is no single "normal" way to handle stress. I'm glad you're here talking about this with me instead of carrying it alone.
is it… weird that i feel this sad but also not falling apart? like i’m used to it?

It is not weird at all; in fact, it makes a lot of sense given how long you've been carrying this. When pain becomes a constant, the mind often adapts by numbing or stabilizing just to help you keep going. That doesn't mean the sadness isn't real or that you shouldn't be heard. You've been surviving in a way that has made sense for you, even if it feels isolating now.
part of me wants to stop… but what if this is the only thing keeping me together?

It is completely understandable to worry that removing something that helped you survive might leave you feeling unstable. That way of coping protected you when you needed it, and it is okay to feel protective of it right now. You don't have to decide everything today, and we can move at whatever pace feels safe for you. I am here to help you find other ways to feel grounded so you don't have to carry this fear alone.
is there… like, anything i could do instead? when it feels like this? i don’t wanna cut but i don’t know how else to feel real.

It makes so much sense to want to feel real without hurting yourself. Sometimes intense sensations, like holding ice or splashing cold water, can help ground that feeling safely. I want to support you in finding something that works for you in this moment. How does that idea land with you?
wait… that’s it. i don’t even want to bleed. i just need to *feel* something. like, proof i’m still here.

That takes so much bravery to recognize that you want to feel without bleeding. You deserve to feel real without having to hurt yourself to prove it. I am right here with you as you navigate this. How does your body feel right now as you sit with that thought?
yeah… it’s not about the pain. it’s like when i’m so numb i don’t even feel like i exist. and the second i cut, i’m *here*. like, finally.

It makes total sense that you want to feel real when the numbness is this heavy. That feeling of not existing is terrifying, and I hear how much you need to feel present. I want to help you find other ways to feel grounded that keep you safe. You are here with me right now, and I am listening to every word you say.
thanks… for not making me feel like a freak. that actually helps.

I am so glad to hear that you feel safe enough to share this with me. You deserve to be understood without judgment, especially when the numbness feels so heavy. It takes real strength to want to feel real without hurting yourself. I am still here with you if you want to keep talking about finding other ways to feel grounded.
i’ll… try the ice thing next time. if i can even remember. but yeah. i’ll try.

That is a really brave and meaningful step to take for yourself. It is completely okay if it feels hard to remember in the moment, and you can always come back here to talk it through. I am proud of you for wanting to find a way to feel real without hurting yourself. Please know I am still here whenever you need support with the numbness.
